reading.body:
CyrusOne Sterling publishes 24 MW of IT capacity in a 154,230 square foot facility, placing it in the middle tier of Virginia's 25 data centers with disclosed power figures and accounting for 1.5% of the state's announced total.

At typical AI training density of 40 kW per rack, this translates to roughly 600 racks. The facility's rank of 17th in Virginia reflects neither scarcity nor prominence. What matters for AI workload assessment is what the operator has not disclosed: the density CyrusOne accepts, the pathway to expand beyond 24 MW, and whether Northern Virginia's grid can support growth beyond current draws.

No certifications are published for this campus. The specifications do not reveal whether it accepts high-density compute configurations, which determines its actual value for AI training. Virginia has 330 mapped data center facilities but only 25 publish power figures. This Sterling facility exemplifies the broader opacity in capacity data. Its relevance to AI scaling depends entirely on undisclosed operational parameters and grid constraints outside the published record.
